reaction.episode: CORRECTION through the Nov 4 close — SPX 7,688.62, only 1.99% off its 120-day high and 5.03% above its 200-day average of $7,320.35, while SMH closed $504.27 in Zone 2 and NVDA $200.13 on the Zone 1 floor, VIX 16.61, HY OAS 3.32 calm, mechanical tally 2 of 4. Today's live tape is much worse — SPY $735.87 down 4.03%, QQQ $651.24 down 5.88%, VIX 26.89 intraday — but the episode state is close-based and no close has printed the zone breaks yet.
reaction.invalidation: The Probe stance is wrong if SMH closes below $470 and NVDA closes below $175 on expanding volume, or if VIX closes above 25 with HY OAS above 4% — either voids the zone thesis and turns the correction into a deeper drawdown regime.

ladder.response: Hold the probe, do not average down into the break — the next zone down is the escalation, and sizing waits for a new zone print and a fresh tally.
ladder.trigger: SMH closes below $470 (Zone 2 floor) or NVDA closes below $175 (Zone 2 floor)

ladder.response: Probe fires on NVDA at Tranche A size (~$541) — the only name still inside its zone; SOXL stays out, its $53 line broke intraday.
ladder.trigger: NVDA closes inside Zone 2 ($175–185) with the capitulation tally at 3 of 6 or better

ladder.response: Treat as the bull trap: do not chase, do not add on the bounce — wait for the failure-zone retest verdict and the second-low test before any further entry.
ladder.trigger: SPX bounces into the 7,750–7,820 failure zone, or SMH into 580–600, and stalls or fails

ladder.response: Stand down — no new probes, ladder void, regime-break conditions met; reassess from cash.
ladder.trigger: VIX closes above 25 or HY OAS closes above 4%

ladder.response: Regime break: the correction thesis is void, stance moves to Watch from cash until a new episode state prints.
ladder.trigger: SPX closes below its 200-day average of $7,320.35

reaction.trapRisk: Today's washout could print the first low near the S&P 500's 200-day average — but the first bounce off a washout low is the trap case in this tape: the Nov 4 session already showed the pattern, index up 1.58% while SMH fell 2.75%. Entries wait for the failure-zone retest verdict or a second low that holds, not for the first green day; the probe fires only on a confirmed Zone 2 close, never intraday.

strategyPosture: Probe, stressed. The Nov 4 close put SMH in Zone 2 with credit calm and a 2-of-4 tally, but today's intraday washout has SMH below the $470 floor, VIX above 25 intraday, and the zone prints unconfirmed until the close — hold the probe, no new entries, no averaging down into the break.

themes.counterRead: The rotation read holds while credit stays loose: the weakness is concentrated in the handful of names that dominate the index by weight, and the index is not confirming a broad rollover. But today the index itself is down 4.03% — the rotation read is under its hardest test, and if lending standards tighten or HY OAS breaks 4%, the rotation read fails and this becomes a rollover. The gap is the signal, not the noise.
themes.dataAnchor: SPY closed Nov 4 at 7,688.62 on the index, down 1.99% from its 120-day trailing high of 7,844.52; live today SPY is $735.87, down 4.03%. The Mag 7 average sits 18.19% below 52-week highs versus SPY at 5.8%, a 12.39-point divergence gap — AAPL is only 3.5% off its high while TSLA is 31.9% off. Bank lending standards are LOOSE at SLOOS 1.7%, far below the ~40% stress threshold.
themes.label: Rotation, Not Rollover
themes.narrative: The tape reads as a broad correction — AI names down 20–50% in a month — yet the index itself was only 1.99% off its 120-day high at the Nov 4 close. The market believes leadership is rotating, not that the market is breaking. Today's 4% index washout is the first day the index itself has joined the drawdown.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS above 4% or SLOOS rising toward 40% voids the rotation read.

themes.counterRead: Prices say the AI cycle is over; revenue says it is still compounding at 55–131%. The gap is the opportunity — but only 2 of 4 mechanical capitulation signals have confirmed (zone occupancy and credit calm), with no volume climax and no VIX rollover yet. And today's tape broke the zone: SMH is below the $470 floor intraday, so a zone print alone is not a bottom call; it is a probe condition, not an all-clear, and the close decides it.
themes.dataAnchor: SMH closed $504.27, inside Zone 2 ($470–505), down 24.94% from its 120-day high and 11.53% below its 50-day average; live today it is below the $470 floor. NVDA is $182.72 live, inside Zone 2 ($175–185), down 24.9% from its high with RSI 25.8. MU is $676.39 live, down 46.1% from its high with RSI 28. Revenue says the opposite of the price: NVDA revenue is growing 61.4% year over year, AVGO 55%, LRCX 131.3%, all with recovery-confirmed inflections, and NVDA carries conviction score 83.
themes.label: AI Infrastructure Washout — Zone Broken Intraday
themes.narrative: The AI bubble is bursting — semiconductors are in free fall, SMH is down 11.17% in five days at the Nov 4 close and has broken below its Zone 2 floor intraday today, and the complex is being abandoned. NVDA fell 8.75% today into Zone 2.
themes.watchFor: SMH close versus the $470 Zone 2 floor; NVDA close inside $175–185 completes the probe condition.

themes.counterRead: The election is a real catalyst, not pure sentiment — the Texas outcome changes the merchant-power math, and a KeyBanc downgrade is a genuine re-rating input. But the price move has overshot the revenue print and insider buying says the trough is being bought, not abandoned. This is a screened candidate to verify, not a chase — the thesis needs confirming before any sizing.
themes.dataAnchor: VST is $112.35 live, down 42.9% from its 52-week high with RSI 29, down 6.34% today after falling 15.82% on Nov 4. VRT is $175.30 live, down 53.9% from its high and down 14.71% today. Against that, VST revenue is still growing 19.1% year over year, insiders bought $1.17M at the trough, and ETN revenue is growing 22.2% year over year. The midterm election event has 36 matched headlines, all on merchant power.
themes.label: AI Power Trade Unwind
themes.narrative: The US midterm election outcome killed the AI power trade — merchant power generators sold off as the market priced policy risk into the nuclear and power buildout, with Vistra plunging on a KeyBanc downgrade and the Texas election vote.
themes.watchFor: VST holding above $110 with insider follow-through, or a second downgrade wave, decides whether this is a trough or a re-rating.

themes.counterRead: The derating is a multiple story, not a cash story — DDOG's 80% gross margin and 29.2% free-cash-flow margin are intact while the price is 41% off its high. If revenue holds, price and fundamentals are moving in opposite directions and this is the setup. If growth decelerates, the multiple is right and the dislocation is a value trap.
themes.dataAnchor: DDOG is $176.84 live, down 41.2% from its high with RSI 26.5, yet revenue is growing 27.7% year over year with an 80% gross margin and $1,001M free cash flow at a 29.2% margin. NET is $237.70, down 35.8% from its high with RSI 28.2 and revenue growing 34.7% year over year. NOW is $102.90, down 41.5% from its high with RSI 28.1; SNOW is $271.44, down 29.4% with RSI 30.7.
themes.label: Software: Cash Generation vs Price
themes.narrative: Software is dead money — AI eats SaaS, the sector is being derated for good, and the multiple compression is permanent.
themes.watchFor: Next prints holding revenue growth above 25% with free-cash-flow margin intact confirm the dislocation; a growth guide-down voids it.

themes.counterRead: Rates and credit agree the stress is equity-concentrated, not systemic — the bond market is not pricing a credit event. But VIX is 26.89 intraday, up 61.89% on the day and above the 25 stand-down line: the stand-down triggers on a close above 25, so the calm read survives only until the close. The December 8–9 FOMC is the dated test of that calm: a hawkish surprise is the path by which calm credit flips.
themes.dataAnchor: The 10-year is 4.95% and the 2-year 4.61%, with the 2s10s curve at +0.34 — not inverted. HY OAS is 3.32, calm and below the 4% stand-down line. VIX closed 16.61 on Nov 4 and is 26.89 live today, up 61.89%. The real 10-year is 2.69%.
themes.label: Credit and Rates Calm — VIX Spike Tests It
themes.narrative: Hot data means more hikes — the December 8–9 FOMC is flagged HIGH signal strength and the market is pricing the Fed signaling higher rates. Credit has not cracked, but the VIX spike is the first intraday breach of the stand-down line in this episode.
themes.watchFor: VIX closing above 25 or HY OAS above 4% breaks the calm read; the Dec 8–9 FOMC is the dated test.

watchFor: SMH close versus the $470 Zone 2 floor and $505 ceiling; NVDA close inside the $175–185 Zone 2 band.
VIX closing above 25 (stand-down) versus rolling over from its 26.89 intraday spike (confirmation).
HY OAS above 4% breaks the credit-calm leg (now 3.32).
SPX closing below its 7,320.35 200-day average voids the correction thesis; a bounce into the 7,750–7,820 failure zone and stalling is the trap case.
SMH volume climax above 1.5x its 20-day average with an intraday reversal (was 1.36x at the Nov 4 close, close in 28% of range).
whereWaveBuilds: The next move builds at the close: either NVDA closes inside Zone 2 ($175–185) with the tally holding and the probe fires on NVDA, or SMH closes below $470 and the zone thesis breaks, opening the next leg down toward the S&P 500's 200-day average at $7,320.35.
